segments.arabic:
١١٧٠٠- لبابة بنت الحارث
بن حزن الهلالية «٣»، أخت التي قبلها، وهي لبابة الصغرى، وأنها تلقب العصماء، وأمها فاختة بنت عامر الثقفية، وهي والدة خالد بن الوليد الصحابي المشهور.
قال أبو عمر: في إسلامها وصحبتها نظر، وأقره ابن الأثير. وهو عجيب، وكأنه استبعده من جهة تقدّم وفاة زوجها الوليد أن تكون ماتت معه أو بعده بقليل، وليس ذلك بلازم، فقد ثبت أنها عاشت بعد وفاة ولدها خالد، ولها في ذلك قصة، فذكر أبو حذيفة في المبتدإ والفتوح عن محمد بن إسحاق قال: لما مات خالد بن الوليد خرج عمر في جنازته فإذا أمّه تندبه وتقول:
أنت خير من ألف ألف من القوم ... إذا ما كنت في وجوه الرّجال
[الخفيف] قال: فقال عمر: صدقت وإن كان لكذلك.
وقال سيف بن عمر في الرّدّة والفتوح بسند له ذكر فيه قصة عزل خالد وإقامته
(١) في أ: سلمة بن أسلم شقيقته.
(٢) أسد الغابة ت (٥٢٥٢)، الاستيعاب ت (٣٥٣٢) .
(٣) أسد الغابة ت (٧٢٥٣)، الاستيعاب ت (٣٥٣٣)، الثقات ٣/ ٣٦١، أعلام النساء ٤/ ١٧٠، ٢٧٢، الكاشف ٣/ ٤٨٠، تجريد أسماء الصحابة ٢/ ٣٠١، تقريب التهذيب ٢/ ٦١٣، تهذيب التهذيب ١٢/ ٤٤٩، تهذيب الكمال ٣/ ١٦٩٧، أزمنة التاريخ الإسلامي ١٠٠٠، خلاصة تهذيب الكمال ٣/ ٣٩٢، ٤٠٥.
segments.english:
11700. Lubaba bint al-Harith

ibn Hazn al-Hilaliyya,[3] the sister of the preceding woman. She was Lubaba the Younger and was surnamed al-Asma'. Her mother was Fakhita bint Amir al-Thaqafiyya. She was the mother of Khalid ibn al-Walid, the famous Companion.

Abu Umar said: “There is reason for doubt concerning her acceptance of Islam and her Companionship.” Ibn al-Athir concurred with him. This is astonishing. It is as though he considered this unlikely because her husband al-Walid had died earlier, supposing that she died with him or shortly thereafter. But that does not necessarily follow. It is established that she lived beyond the death of her son Khalid, and there is an account concerning this.

Abu Hudhayfa related in al-Mubtada' wa-al-Futuh, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: When Khalid ibn al-Walid died, Umar went out in his funeral procession, and there was his mother lamenting him and saying:

You are better than a thousand thousand of the people …
When you were among the foremost men.

[al-Khafif meter]

He said: Umar then said, “You have spoken the truth; indeed, he was so.”

Sayf ibn Umar said in al-Ridda wa-al-Futuh, with an isnad of his in which he mentioned the account of Khalid's dismissal and his residence—

[1] In manuscript A: “Salama ibn Aslam, her full brother.”

[2] Usd al-Ghaba, entry 5252; al-Isti'ab, entry 3532.

[3] Usd al-Ghaba, entry 7253; al-Isti'ab, entry 3533; al-Thiqat, 3/361; A'lam al-Nisa', 4/170, 272; al-Kashif, 3/480; al-Tajrid, 2/301; Taqrib al-Tahdhib, 2/613; Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, 12/449; Tahdhib al-Kamal, 3/1697; Azminat al-Tarikh al-Islami, 1000; Khulasat Tahdhib al-Kamal, 3/392, 405.

segments.arabic:
بالمدينة، قال: فلما رأى عمر أنه قد زال ما كان يخشاه من افتتان الناس به عزم على أن يوليه بعد أن يرجع من الحجّ، فخرج معه خالد بن الوليد، فاستسقى خارجا من المدينة، فقال: احدروني إلى مهاجري، فقدمت به أمه المدينة ومرضته حتى ثقل، فلقي عمر لاق وهو راجع من الحجّ، فقال له: ما الخبر؟ فقال: خالد لما به، فطوى عمر ثلاثا في ليلة فأدركه حين قضى، فرّق عليه واسترجع، فلما جهز بكته البواكي. قيل له: ألا تنهاهن! فقال: وما على نساء قريش أن تبكين أبا سليمان ما لم يكن نقع أو لقلقة «١» . فلما أخرج بجنازته إذا امرأة محرمة تبكيه وتقول: أنت خير من ألف ألف ... البيت المتقدم، وبعده:
أشجاع فأنت أشجع من ليث ... صهر ابن جهم أبي أشبال
أجواد فأنت أجود من سيل ... أتى يستقلّ بين الجبال
[الخفيف] فقال عمر: من هذه؟ فقيل: أمه. فقال: أمه، والإله- ثلاثا، وهل قامت النساء عن مثل خالد!.
وهذا وإن كان من رواية أبي حذيفة وهو ضعيف، وكذلك سيف، لكن قد ذكر ابن سعد وهو ثقة عن كثير بن هشام، عن جعفر بن برقان، عن يزيد بن الأصم، قال: لما توفي خالد بن الوليد بكت عليه أمّه، فقال عمر: يا أم خالد، أخالدا أو أجره ترزئين! عزمت عليك إلا تثبت، حتى تسود يداك من الخضاب.
وهذا مسند صحيح، وعلق البخاري قول عمر في النّقع واللقلقة في البكاء على خالد، لكن لم يسمّ أمّه.
ومجموع ذلك يفيد أنها عاشت بعد النبي ﵌، أفيظن بها أنها استمرت على الكفر من بعد الفتح إلى أن مات النبي ﵌؟ هذا بعيد عادة، بل يبطله ما تقدم أنه لم يبق بالحرمين ولا الطائف أحد في حجة الوداع إلا أسلم وشهدها.
segments.english:
In Medina. He said: When Umar saw that what he had feared—people becoming infatuated with Khalid—had passed, he resolved to appoint him after he returned from the pilgrimage. Khalid ibn al-Walid set out with him. Outside Medina, Khalid developed dropsy and said, “Take me down to the place of my emigration.” His mother brought him to Medina and nursed him until he became gravely ill. As Umar was returning from the pilgrimage, someone met him. He asked, “What is the news?” The man replied, “Khalid is in a grievous condition.” Umar covered three [stages] in a single night and reached him just as he died. He was moved by his death and recited, “Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return.” When he had been prepared for burial, the mourning women lamented him. Umar was asked, “Will you not forbid them?” He replied, “What harm is there if the women of Quraysh weep for Abu Sulayman, so long as there is neither dust-raising nor clamorous wailing?”¹

When his bier was brought out, there was a woman in ihram weeping for him and saying:

“You are better than a thousand thousand …”

—the verse quoted above—and after it:

“Brave? You are braver than a lion—
The in-law of Ibn Jahm, a father of cubs.
Generous? You are more generous than a torrent
That comes surging between the mountains.”

[al-Khafif]

Umar asked, “Who is this?” He was told, “His mother.” He said three times, “His mother, by Allah! Have women ever given birth to the like of Khalid?”

Although this comes through the transmission of Abu Hudhayfa, who is weak, as is Sayf, Ibn Sa'd—who is trustworthy—also reported from Kathir ibn Hisham, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, who said: When Khalid ibn al-Walid died, his mother wept over him. Umar said, “O Umm Khalid, is it Khalid or his reward that you would be bereaved of? I adjure you to persist until your hands have been blackened with dye.”

This is a sound report with a fully connected chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari quoted in suspended form Umar’s statement concerning dust-raising and clamorous wailing during the weeping over Khalid, but he did not name Khalid’s mother.

Taken together, this indicates that she lived after the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Is she then to be thought to have remained an unbeliever from after the Conquest until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, died? That is normally far-fetched. Indeed, it is refuted by what was stated previously: that by the Farewell Pilgrimage no one remained in the Two Holy Sanctuaries or al-Ta'if who had not embraced Islam and attended it.

unresolved.explanation: The canonical text clearly reads محرمة, rendered “in ihram,” whereas a collateral recension reads محتزمة, “girded.” The canonical reading governs, but the manuscript-level relationship between the readings remains undetermined.

The canonical wording is translated literally as “the in-law of Ibn Jahm, a father of cubs,” despite its anomalous sense. Collateral reports preserve different lion imagery, but they are not manuscripts of al-Isabah and therefore cannot justify silently replacing the canonical line.

unresolved.explanation: The canonical wording is syntactically difficult and has been rendered conservatively. Ibn Sa'd’s collateral report reads ألا تبيتي and refers to not letting the night pass, but that wording is absent from the authoritative current Arabic and has not been imported into the translation.
